title: RBI Survey of Professional Forecasters: CPI Inflation
description: Median forecast of annual headline CPI (Combined) inflation (per cent) by professional forecasters in the Reserve Bank's Survey of Professional Forecasters. Each point is the median forecast of the panel in one survey round, stamped on the first day of the month in which the survey was conducted (the press release follows 4-6 weeks later). The 'current fiscal year' series is the forecast for the April-March year that contains the survey month (e.g. a September 2026 round gives 2026-27); 'next fiscal year' is the following year. So the series is the evolution of expectations, not a time series of outcomes: the forecast target changes each April. Compare with the RBI's own projection and the inflation target (4 per cent, with a 2-6 per cent tolerance band).
source: Reserve Bank of India (Survey of Professional Forecasters press releases)

qna.question: What does this series show?
qna.answer: The panel's median forecast for average headline CPI inflation (CPI Combined, general index) over the fiscal year, from each round of the Survey of Professional Forecasters.^The first series is the forecast for the year in which the survey was conducted, the second for the next year.

qna.question: How do I read the points?
qna.answer: The date is the survey month, the value the forecast. Rising forecasts across rounds mean forecasters are marking up inflation; a gap between current-year and next-year forecasts signals the expected path.^The press release also gives quarterly CPI forecasts, core CPI and WPI forecasts, not included here.

qna.question: What are the caveats?
qna.answer: CPI was rebased (2024=100) recently, so forecasts made on the old and new index are not strictly comparable. Fiscal-year inflation is an annual average, so a forecast for the current year partly reflects months already published.^Forecasts are the panellists' own and the panel changes from round to round.
